title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
why_read: A dense theoretical paper probing when integrated information, a mechanism-level quantity tied to theories of consciousness, can actually be measured reliably from limited experimental data.
analysis: The paper examines integrated information theory's φ measure, which tries to quantify how much a system's internal mechanism integrates information beyond what its input-output behavior alone would suggest. It shows that two networks with identical observable behavior can have very different internal φ values, meaning behavior alone can't tell you which one actually has more 'integration,' but that enough targeted internal measurements can distinguish them within a small number of trials. It also demonstrates that the measure is fragile, since tiny changes in the underlying mechanism can shift φ by 25 to 100 percent at most measured boundary cases, and that near-perfect model fits can still misreport φ by over 20 percent. This is a rigorous, mathematically careful contribution relevant to AI interpretability and consciousness research, though it's a niche topic requiring background in interventional causal analysis to fully appreciate.
